name: CanonicalWireframe Dependency Rules
principles: Entity and Property are the only canonical atoms.
Every Node is an abstraction; families are predefined abstraction contracts.
ABS is the least opinionated standard family.
Properties are unbounded and NodeType reads are not whitelists.
Function, Event, Effect, Data, Schema, Asset, Members and Required Link are Properties.
function_call and logic op=call are forbidden.
Assets are opaque payloads; canonical meaning remains in Entity + Property.
Property ownership and Link endpoint semantics are separate concerns.
Runtime state belongs to an execution context and does not mutate the canonical Model artifact.

entity_ref.rule: An Entity reference MUST resolve to exactly one active Entity.id in Model/.

property_ref.identity_rule: Every active Property.id MUST be unique across the complete Model/ closure.
property_ref.resolution_rule: A bare canonical Property reference MUST resolve by exact Property.id across the complete Model/ closure.
property_ref.owner_rule: The owning Entity is the Entity whose properties[] contains the resolved Property definition. Consumers MUST NOT infer Property ownership from Property naming, file location, endpoint direction or convention.
property_ref.ambiguity_rule: Zero matches or more than one match is invalid. No local-first, nearest-file, family-local or naming-convention fallback is permitted.

data_state_model.canonical_role: A Data Property defines a typed runtime slot contract and its canonical initial binding marker.
data_state_model.runtime_scope: Runtime Data values are held per execution context. Reads, writes, Event conditions, caused Events and Effects operate within the same execution context unless another contract explicitly states otherwise.

states.UNBOUND: value is null. UNBOUND is not a schema violation and does not satisfy ready conditions.
states.READY: value is non-null and, when schema_ref is present, the value conforms to that Schema.
states.INVALID: a non-null binding candidate fails its Schema or another declared Data constraint. INVALID does not satisfy ready conditions.

data_state_model.binding_rule: Schema required-field constraints apply only to non-null binding candidates. A canonical value:null therefore represents an unbound slot rather than an invalid record.
data_state_model.package_validation_rule: A valid package or valid Data slot contract MUST NOT be interpreted as a READY runtime Data value. READY exists only for a concrete execution-context binding after runtime validation.
data_state_model.mutation_rule: Runtime write/bind operations change execution-context state only; they MUST NOT rewrite the canonical .cw artifact.

schema_semantics.record: definition.fields declares field contracts; required applies when validating a non-null record value.
schema_semantics.string: a non-null value MUST be a string.
schema_semantics.integer: a non-null value MUST be an integer value and MUST NOT be a boolean value.
schema_semantics.list: definition.item_schema_ref declares the item Schema. definition.unique_by optionally names an item field whose non-null values MUST be unique. definition.required_items optionally requires list items matching explicit field/value pairs.
schema_semantics.map: a non-null value MUST be a string-keyed mapping. definition.value_schema_ref declares the Schema that every map value MUST satisfy.
schema_semantics.required_items: Each required_items entry has field and value. A conforming list MUST contain at least one item whose named field equals the declared value.
schema_semantics.runtime_boundary: Opaque Asset payload contents are not parsed by the CW package validator. An adapter/runtime that binds payload-derived values into Data slots MUST validate the resulting non-null value against schema_ref before the slot becomes READY.

event_execution_model.context: Every Event occurrence belongs to one execution context and caused Events preserve that context.
event_execution_model.condition_rule: event_condition Links are guards on an Event occurrence, not independent Event sources.
event_execution_model.pending_rule: An emitted Event occurrence with unsatisfied conditions remains pending in its execution context. It dispatches exactly once when all its conditions become satisfied.
event_execution_model.no_replay_rule: Condition transitions do not create additional Event occurrences. One emit creates at most one dispatch.
event_execution_model.handler_rule: When an Event occurrence dispatches, its linked handler/effect semantics execute in the same context.

function_interface_model.input_refs: Function.input_refs is the exact set of canonical Property refs read by that Function's modeled logic. Execution-context Data visible around the Function is not an input unless the Function actually reads it.
function_interface_model.output_refs: Function.output_refs is the exact set of canonical Property refs written/produced by that Function's modeled logic.
function_interface_model.relay_rule: A Function may have empty input_refs and output_refs when its modeled purpose is purely causal control such as emitting another Event.
function_interface_model.validation_rule: Generic tooling SHOULD verify that modeled canonical reads are declared in input_refs, modeled canonical writes are declared in output_refs, and unused declared refs are rejected unless another explicit Function contract permits them.

link_property_model.ownership: A Link is a Property and is owned by exactly one Entity through ordinary Entity.properties[] containment.
link_property_model.declarer_semantics: The owning Entity is the declarer of the relation: it canonically asserts that the Link exists. Link ownership is therefore meaningful even though it is independent from endpoint direction.
link_property_model.endpoint_semantics: parent_ref and child_ref define the semantic endpoints of the Link independently of which Entity owns the Link Property.
link_property_model.cross_entity_rule: A Link Property MAY connect Properties or Entities owned by other Entities. Link ownership MUST NOT be interpreted as an implicit endpoint.
link_property_model.storage_rule: Moving a Link Property between Entity.properties[] collections changes its declarer and is therefore a canonical semantic change; it MUST NOT be done merely to imitate endpoint direction.
link_property_model.validation_rule: Link validity is determined from the resolved endpoint refs and the selected Link Ruleset, not from co-location with either endpoint.

node_ruleset.rule: A valid Property remains valid even when its Property type is not present in effective reads.

constraints: self_endpoint MUST be parent_ref or child_ref.
min MUST be a non-negative integer.
max, when present, MUST be an integer greater than or equal to min.
A Link.required_link_ref MUST resolve to exactly one required_link Property.
The Required Link Property MUST be owned by the Entity occupying the Link endpoint selected by self_endpoint.
schema_type_ref MUST name exactly one value registered in schema_types.
Any schema_ref, item_schema_ref or value_schema_ref inside definition MUST resolve to a Property whose property_type_ref is schema.
For schema_type_ref=list, unique_by when present MUST name a field in the item record Schema.
For schema_type_ref=list, required_items when present MUST be an array of explicit field/value requirements.
For schema_type_ref=map, definition.value_schema_ref is required and MUST resolve to the Schema for every map value.
schema_ref, when present, MUST resolve to a Property whose property_type_ref is schema.
value:null means UNBOUND and is valid as a slot state regardless of required fields in schema_ref.
A non-null runtime binding becomes READY only after schema validation succeeds.
input_refs and output_refs, when present, MUST resolve through canonical Property reference resolution.
input_refs describe canonical Properties actually read by modeled Function logic, not all Data visible in the execution context.
output_refs describe canonical Properties actually written or produced by modeled Function logic.

link_rulesets.rule: dependency is structural only and MUST NOT imply causal execution.
The Link Property may be owned by any canonical Entity. Causal source identity is parent_ref, not Link Property ownership.
condition_mode=ready is satisfied exactly when parent_ref resolves to a Data Property in READY state in the Event occurrence execution context.

effect_types.rule: On dispatch, copy the single input Data value to every explicitly linked effect_target in the same execution context without changing canonical identity.

semantics.read: Read a canonical Data/Property value in the current execution context by exact ref; optional path selects a nested value.
semantics.write: Write a value to the canonical target Data/Property slot in the current execution context. Non-null Data writes MUST satisfy schema_ref before the slot becomes READY.
semantics.assign: Bind a transient local_ref inside the containing Function.logic execution scope.
semantics.lookup: Read one item from a READY collection. The source MUST be READY before lookup executes; lookup against UNBOUND or INVALID source is INVALID execution, never null. For a list, key_field selects the compared item field and key is matched by exact equality; zero matches in a READY collection returns null and more than one match is INVALID. A list Schema unique_by constraint can guarantee at most one match.
semantics.concat: Concatenate ordered scalar/string expressions into one scalar/string value.
semantics.emit: cause_ref MUST resolve to an event_cause Link whose parent_ref resolves to the containing Function Property.id. The emitted Event occurrence preserves the current execution context.
semantics.return: Return from local Function logic; return alone does not create cross-Function causality.
semantics.fail: Terminate the current Function execution as INVALID using an explicit machine-readable code. fail MUST NOT emit subsequent Events from the terminated control path.
semantics.if: Select exactly one local logic branch from an explicit boolean condition.
